messages:
morgan: heads-up — spotted a regression where a user with 'viewer' org role + membership in a group with 'team-admin' on a project was able to SAVE project settings in the Console. repro steps below. @eva-sec @lee-frontend

morgan: repro steps: 1) create user U with role=viewer at org level; 2) add U to group G that has role=team-admin scoped to project P; 3) log in as U -> Console -> Projects -> P -> Settings -> change retention days -> Save -> change persists. Not expected.

lee-frontend: thanks for flagging. Is this frontend gating or server-side permission eval? Could be a missing server check after the role-refactor.

anya-backend: likely server-side. We flattened role resolution in the 2050008xxx refactor and added an "effective_permissions" cache. There was a short-circuit where group-derived grants bypassed additional write checks.

chris-sre: logs show a spike of 200 responses for POST /api/projects/:id/settings around deploy 2050009000. Before that it returned 403 for the same requests.

eva-sec: hold on rollback until we confirm blast radius. Triage plan: 1) run audit log query for project.update actions, 2) enumerate affected orgs/users, 3) if widespread, temporarily revoke group grants or add a deny policy.

morgan: pulled a sample org (org-142) — found 3 users who performed project.update via UI. Audit entries: action=project.update, actor_id=U-338, session=web-... , ts=2050011202. Stacktrace looks like permission check returned true upstream. Code snippet from permission eval:```python
def has_write(user, project):
    perms = effective_permissions(user)  # includes groups
    if perms.get('project.write'):
        return True
    # the bug: group grants were inserted here without context check
    return False
```

lee-frontend: frontend gating uses canEditProject computed from /api/me/effective-perms and shows Save button if true. So if the server endpoint overstates perms, both frontend and server-side UI will appear to allow the action. We need the server to be canonical.

priya-pm: any known customer impact? Support tickets?

morgan: one support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting they changed retention accidentally. No secret material exfil yet, but project config drift is bad.

eva-sec: KMS question — could this allow changing which KMS key a project points to or editing key policies? That would be higher severity. Who can change key bindings today?

anya-backend: KMS admin actions are guarded in kms-service by is_kms_admin(user). The project settings endpoint accepts a kms_key_id field. Bug allowed non-kms-admins to change the kms_key_id pointer for a project (i.e., swap which key the project uses) — it doesn't let them touch key policies but it can point project to a different key.

morgan: proposed quick mitigation: require explicit project.admin (not group-derived) or require a separate "project.write:allow" check for any update to kms_key_id. Also add middleware fast-reject when action implies changing sensitive fields.

chris-sre: I'll add a detection rule: alert on project.update where actor.role == viewer in last 24h and on any change to kms_key_id. Can create a canary alert channel.

devops-bot: deploy scheduled: hotfix branch -> canary window 2050015000 to 2050016000. Owner: @anya-backend. Rollback window 30m.

priya-pm: mark as P2, notify support and CS to reach out to affected customers. Draft short note: "We found a permission regression affecting project settings; we are patching and will list affected projects."

eva-sec: agreed. Post-patch actions: 1) run KMS pointer audit for last 30 days and list changes, 2) if any unexpected key swaps, rotate keys as precaution, 3) open vulnerability triage — looks like app logic, not third-party CVE, but document findings.

morgan: patch merged to release branch, canary started. I'll follow up with exact SQL to list affected project rows and a short mitigation playbook for support. Thanks all :thumbsup:
